segments.text: Every week we perform hundreds of different tasks in our laboratories.
segments.zh: 每周我们都要在实验室里完成数百项不同的任务。

segments.text: This work is performed at different workstations, using different instruments and materials,
segments.zh: 这些工作在不同的工作台上进行，使用不同的仪器和材料，

segments.text: and employing different movements.
segments.zh: 并采用不同的动作。

segments.text: As a result, each task makes a different set of demands on our bodies.
segments.zh: 因此，每项任务对我们身体的要求都不一样。

segments.text: If we aren't careful, some of them can lead to unhealthy stress or strain.
segments.zh: 如果我们不小心，其中一些就可能导致不健康的压力或劳损。

segments.text: The science of ergonomics helps us to take a look at these situations and determine
segments.zh: 人机工效学帮助我们审视这些情况，并确定

segments.text: what we need to do to avoid any harmful effects.
segments.zh: 我们需要做些什么来避免任何有害影响。

segments.text: It does this by examining our job, work area, instruments, and tools.
segments.zh: 它通过审视我们的工作、工作区域、仪器和工具来做到这一点。

segments.text: Ergonomics shows us how to adapt what we do to our own physical makeup so we can work effectively,
segments.zh: 人机工效学告诉我们如何让自己所做的事情适应自身的身体条件，从而高效地工作，

segments.text: and most importantly, safely.
segments.zh: 而且最重要的是，安全地工作。

segments.text: Are you short or tall?
segments.zh: 你个子矮还是高？

segments.text: Do you have long legs?
segments.zh: 你的腿长吗？

segments.text: What about your arms?
segments.zh: 你的手臂呢？

segments.text: Physical size and shape are important considerations when designing work areas and equipment.
segments.zh: 在设计工作区域和设备时，身体的尺寸和体型是重要的考虑因素。

segments.text: To work safely, we need to minimize the amount of stress we place on our bodies.
segments.zh: 要安全地工作，我们需要尽量减少施加在身体上的压力。

segments.text: The design engineers who develop workstations and other lab equipment try to make them work
segments.zh: 开发工作台和其他实验室设备的设计工程师，会尽力让它们

segments.text: well for everyone.
segments.zh: 适合每一个人。

segments.text: Since this is pretty much impossible, they do their best to come close by designing them
segments.zh: 由于这几乎是不可能的，他们就尽量接近这个目标，把它们设计得

segments.text: to fit most people.
segments.zh: 适合大多数人。

segments.text: Customizing your work area so that it works best for you becomes a job for you and your
segments.zh: 调整你的工作区域，使它最适合你，这就成了你和你的

segments.text: supervisor.
segments.zh: 主管的任务。

segments.text: How closely you match up with your workplace will determine how hard your muscles and joints
segments.zh: 你与工作场所的匹配程度，将决定你在工作时

segments.text: will be asked to work while you're on the job.
segments.zh: 肌肉和关节要承受多大的负担。

segments.text: To start, think about arranging your instruments and materials so you're not forced to make
segments.zh: 首先，要考虑如何摆放你的仪器和材料，使你不必被迫做出

segments.text: unhealthy movements such as overstretching.
segments.zh: 过度伸展之类的不健康动作。

segments.text: You also want to avoid long sessions of repetitive motion without rest, irregular and extreme
segments.zh: 你还要避免长时间不休息地重复动作、不规则和极端的

segments.text: motions, overly heavy loads, and using the wrong tool for the job.
segments.zh: 动作、过重的负荷，以及使用不适合工作的工具。

segments.text: These are the main contributors to ergonomic health problems.
segments.zh: 这些是导致人机工效健康问题的主要因素。

segments.text: Practicing positive work techniques whenever possible is one thing that can help us with
segments.zh: 尽可能采用良好的工作方法，是帮助我们应对

segments.text: these problems.
segments.zh: 这些问题的方法之一。

segments.text: This includes performing stretching exercises to relieve muscle tension and doing our best
segments.zh: 这包括做伸展运动来缓解肌肉紧张，并尽量

segments.text: to keep our bodies in neutral, non-stressful positions.
segments.zh: 让身体保持在中立、无压力的姿势。

segments.text: Neutral positions put the least stress possible on our body.
segments.zh: 中立姿势对身体造成的压力最小。

segments.text: Each major joint and muscle group has its own neutral position.
segments.zh: 每个主要关节和肌群都有各自的中立姿势。

segments.text: We'll start with the wrist.
segments.zh: 我们从手腕说起。

segments.text: Keep your wrist straight, as if you were about to shake hands with someone.
segments.zh: 保持手腕伸直，就像你要和别人握手时那样。

segments.text: This position creates the least amount of stress, and you should use it whenever possible.
segments.zh: 这个姿势产生的压力最小，你应该尽可能采用它。

segments.text: You'll find that other wrist positions are significantly more stressful, especially when
segments.zh: 你会发现，手腕的其他姿势压力要大得多，尤其是

segments.text: they're used over long periods of time.
segments.zh: 长时间保持的时候。

segments.text: There's also a neutral position to help your arms and shoulders.
segments.zh: 手臂和肩膀也有一个中立姿势。

segments.text: If you're working at a lab bench, try to keep your upper arms to the side and your
segments.zh: 如果你在实验台前工作，尽量让上臂贴在身体两侧，

segments.text: forearms at 90 degree angles.
segments.zh: 前臂成 90 度角。

segments.text: This puts the least amount of stress on these joints and muscles.
segments.zh: 这样对这些关节和肌肉造成的压力最小。

segments.text: It may not seem like there are many opportunities to use neutral positions, but in reality,
segments.zh: 看起来可能没有多少机会采用中立姿势，但实际上，

segments.text: there are a lot.
segments.zh: 机会有很多。

segments.text: Paying attention to workstation height is one of the keys.
segments.zh: 注意工作台的高度是关键之一。

segments.text: You need to fine-tune your workstation to fit your physical characteristics.
segments.zh: 你需要微调你的工作台，使它适合你的身体特征。

segments.text: Keep your work surfaces at a height that makes it easy to maintain neutral arm positioning.
segments.zh: 让工作台面保持在一个便于手臂维持中立姿势的高度。

segments.text: You may need to raise or lower your chair to get the best position possible.
segments.zh: 你可能需要升高或降低椅子，以获得尽可能好的姿势。

segments.text: If you're standing and need to get higher, use a small step stool or platform, or see
segments.zh: 如果你是站着的并且需要更高一些，可以用一个小踏凳或平台，或者看看

segments.text: if you can lower the work surface.
segments.zh: 能否降低工作台面。

segments.text: As we've said, careful positioning of your tools and materials is important to good ergonomic
segments.zh: 正如我们说过的，仔细摆放你的工具和材料，对于良好的人机工效

segments.text: health as well.
segments.zh: 健康也很重要。

segments.text: Keep them in front of your body as much as possible.
segments.zh: 尽量把它们放在身体的正前方。

segments.text: This will encourage neutral movements.
segments.zh: 这样有助于做出中立的动作。

segments.text: Never put supplies where you have to stretch to reach them, especially if you need to support
segments.zh: 绝不要把用品放在需要伸长身子才能够到的地方，尤其是当你需要

segments.text: yourself with one hand to grab your materials with the other.
segments.zh: 用一只手撑住自己、用另一只手去拿材料的时候。

segments.text: Avoid other stretching and twisting movements, and don't put yourself in cramped positions
segments.zh: 避免其他伸展和扭转动作，也不要让自己处于局促的姿势，

segments.text: that will prevent your body from moving efficiently.
segments.zh: 那会妨碍身体有效地活动。

segments.text: Another ergonomic problem involves repetition, such as extending your arms in the same way
segments.zh: 另一个人机工效问题与重复有关，比如长时间以同样的方式

segments.text: over and over again for long periods of time.
segments.zh: 一遍又一遍地伸出手臂。

segments.text: Repetition can lead to fatigue, which is a signal that your body needs some relief.
segments.zh: 重复会导致疲劳，而疲劳是身体需要缓一缓的信号。

segments.text: To guard against this, vary your work patterns when you can, and take periodic mini-breaks
segments.zh: 为防止这种情况，尽可能变换工作方式，并定期做短暂休息，

segments.text: to loosen tight muscles.
segments.zh: 放松紧绷的肌肉。

segments.text: Never use excessive force to perform a task.
segments.zh: 绝不要用过大的力气去完成一项任务。

segments.text: Applying a lot of pressure to any part of your body can lead to an injury, especially
segments.zh: 对身体任何部位施加很大的压力都可能导致受伤，尤其是

segments.text: if you're not in a neutral position.
segments.zh: 在你没有处于中立姿势的时候。

segments.text: Much of the lab work we perform is done with gloves.
segments.zh: 我们所做的很多实验室工作都要戴手套。

segments.text: Choosing a pair with the right fit is essential to ergonomic safety.
segments.zh: 选择一副合手的手套，对于人机工效安全至关重要。

segments.text: Gloves that are too large or too thick force you to grip objects tightly, which can lead
segments.zh: 太大或太厚的手套会迫使你用力抓握物体，这可能导致

segments.text: to painful swelling of your tendons.
segments.zh: 肌腱疼痛肿胀。

segments.text: Gloves that are too tight or are stiff at the wrist can press on nerves, blood vessels,
segments.zh: 太紧或手腕处太硬的手套会压迫神经、血管

segments.text: and the carpal tunnel, again leading to serious injuries.
segments.zh: 和腕管，同样会导致严重伤害。

segments.text: So make sure you select gloves that are comfortable and that fit you well for the work you're
segments.zh: 所以一定要选择舒适、合手、适合你正在

segments.text: performing.
segments.zh: 做的工作的手套。

segments.text: There are also ergonomic issues involving your eyes.
segments.zh: 还有涉及眼睛的人机工效问题。

segments.text: For instance, working for long hours at a microscope or computer can lead to an uncomfortable
segments.zh: 例如，长时间在显微镜或电脑前工作，可能会导致令人不适的

segments.text: case of eye strain.
segments.zh: 眼疲劳。

segments.text: To avoid this, take a comfort break.
segments.zh: 为避免这种情况，要做一下舒缓休息。

segments.text: Close your eyes and rest them for a minute.
segments.zh: 闭上眼睛，让它们休息一分钟。

segments.text: One technique is to cover them with the palms of your hands.
segments.zh: 一种方法是用手掌把眼睛盖住。

segments.text: Do this periodically to keep your eyes feeling fresh.
segments.zh: 定期这样做，让眼睛保持清爽。

segments.text: An exercise called refocusing can often help as well.
segments.zh: 一种叫做重新聚焦的练习通常也会有帮助。

segments.text: Move your eyes away from your equipment to something more distant, like a point outside
segments.zh: 把视线从设备上移开，看向更远的地方，比如窗外

segments.text: your window or across the lab.
segments.zh: 或实验室另一头的某一点。

segments.text: Stay focused on this point for 60 to 90 seconds.
segments.zh: 盯住这一点 60 到 90 秒。

segments.text: Both of these practices allow your eye muscles to relax, back to a more normal state before
segments.zh: 这两种做法都能让眼部肌肉放松，恢复到更正常的状态，然后

segments.text: you return to the close-in focus of your work.
segments.zh: 你再回到工作中的近距离聚焦。

segments.text: Your back and neck are especially vulnerable to ergonomic problems.
segments.zh: 你的背部和颈部特别容易出现人机工效问题。

segments.text: You need to consider them both when working in the lab.
segments.zh: 在实验室工作时，你需要同时顾及这两者。

segments.text: Stress to either can lead to painful injuries.
segments.zh: 任何一处受到压力都可能导致疼痛的损伤。

segments.text: Your back can be weakened in many ways through improper lifting, a fall, even bad posture.
segments.zh: 你的背部可能因为很多原因而受损，比如不正确的搬举、摔倒，甚至不良姿势。

segments.text: As with the rest of your body, you also need to keep your back and neck in a neutral
segments.zh: 和身体其他部位一样，你也需要让背部和颈部保持中立的

segments.text: straight position.
segments.zh: 挺直姿势。

segments.text: That means no unusual bending or twisting.
segments.zh: 这意味着不要有异常的弯腰或扭转。

segments.text: Believe it or not, sitting is one of the most stressful positions for your back.
segments.zh: 信不信由你，坐姿是对背部压力最大的姿势之一。

segments.text: Remember to sit so that your lower back, its lumbar region, is comfortably supported by
segments.zh: 记住坐的时候要让你的下背部，也就是腰部区域，舒适地靠在

segments.text: the padding of your chair.
segments.zh: 椅子的软垫上。

segments.text: Keep both feet flat on the floor, knees slightly higher than your hips.
segments.zh: 双脚平放在地面上，膝盖略高于臀部。

segments.text: This position places the least stress on your back.
segments.zh: 这个姿势对背部造成的压力最小。

segments.text: To get the best lumbar support, you may need to adjust your chair or place a pillow
segments.zh: 为了获得最好的腰部支撑，你可能需要调整椅子，或者在背后放一个枕头

segments.text: or rolled-up towel behind your back.
segments.zh: 或卷起来的毛巾。

segments.text: If your feet tend to dangle, you should rest them on a book or platform.
segments.zh: 如果你的脚容易悬空，应该把脚搁在一本书或一个平台上。

segments.text: While they're better than they used to be, many lab stools still lack good lumbar support.
segments.zh: 虽然比过去好了，但很多实验凳仍然缺乏良好的腰部支撑。

segments.text: Here, shifting your hips forward will help to keep you from hunching over.
segments.zh: 这时，把臀部往前挪一挪，有助于避免你弓着背。

segments.text: Again, a towel or pillow may be helpful too.
segments.zh: 同样，毛巾或枕头也可能有帮助。

segments.text: Use the stool's rails as foot rests and take frequent stretches to loosen up tight
segments.zh: 把凳子的横档当作脚踏，并经常做伸展，放松紧绷的

segments.text: muscles.
segments.zh: 肌肉。

segments.text: Standing can be just as tiring to your back as it is to your feet and legs.
segments.zh: 站立对背部造成的疲劳，和对脚和腿造成的一样多。

segments.text: Again, organize your tools and materials ahead of time so that everything's well
segments.zh: 同样，要提前整理好你的工具和材料，让所有东西都在

segments.text: within reach.
segments.zh: 伸手可及的范围内。

segments.text: Avoid bending and stooping.
segments.zh: 避免弯腰和俯身。

segments.text: Keep comfort in mind when you're standing for long periods of time.
segments.zh: 长时间站立时要注意舒适。

segments.text: Shift your weight from one foot to the other.
segments.zh: 把身体重心在两只脚之间来回转移。

segments.text: Using a foot rest to keep one foot higher than the other can also help to
segments.zh: 用脚踏让一只脚比另一只脚高一些，也有助于

segments.text: take some of the load off your back.
segments.zh: 减轻背部的一些负担。

segments.text: Wear comfortable shoes with cushioned insoles and stand on cushioned anti-fatigue mats
segments.zh: 穿带有缓冲鞋垫的舒适鞋子，并站在有缓冲的防疲劳垫上，

segments.text: if they're available.
segments.zh: 如果有的话。

segments.text: You'll be amazed at how much difference these types of things can make.
segments.zh: 你会惊讶于这些做法能带来多大的不同。

segments.text: Proper lifting techniques are essential to the health of your back and neck.
segments.zh: 正确的搬举方法对于背部和颈部的健康至关重要。

segments.text: Before lifting an object, examine it to make sure you're not biting off more
segments.zh: 在搬起一件物体之前，先查看一下，确保你不是在

segments.text: than you can chew.
segments.zh: 做力所不及的事。

segments.text: If you can safely lift the object yourself, first get close to it.
segments.zh: 如果你能安全地自己搬起这件物体，首先要靠近它。

segments.text: Keeping your back straight, bend slowly at the knees.
segments.zh: 保持背部挺直，慢慢屈膝下蹲。

segments.text: Don't bend at the waist.
segments.zh: 不要弯腰。

segments.text: Get a good grip on the sides of the object.
segments.zh: 牢牢抓住物体的两侧。

segments.text: Lift slowly with your legs, keeping your back straight and balancing the load on
segments.zh: 用腿部力量慢慢抬起，保持背部挺直，并让负荷平衡地靠在

segments.text: your chest.
segments.zh: 胸前。

segments.text: When walking with an object, remember not to twist your back.
segments.zh: 搬着物体行走时，记住不要扭转背部。

segments.text: Turn with your feet instead and always keep the object close to you.
segments.zh: 而是用脚转身，并始终让物体靠近身体。

segments.text: This also helps to reduce the strain on your back.
segments.zh: 这也有助于减轻背部的劳损。

segments.text: To set the object down, simply follow the rules in reverse.
segments.zh: 要放下物体，只需把这些规则反过来做。

segments.text: Keep your back straight, bend with your knees and set the object down carefully.
segments.zh: 保持背部挺直，屈膝，小心地把物体放下。

segments.text: If something's too heavy or awkward to handle, don't risk an injury.
segments.zh: 如果东西太重或不便搬运，不要冒受伤的风险。

segments.text: Get help.
segments.zh: 去找人帮忙，

segments.text: Lift the object together.
segments.zh: 一起搬起物体。

segments.text: Counting out loud is often helpful.
segments.zh: 大声数数通常很有帮助。

segments.text: If there's no one around to help or the load is too heavy for two people to carry,
segments.zh: 如果周围没有人帮忙，或者负荷太重、两个人也搬不动，

segments.text: get a cart or dolly.
segments.zh: 就用推车或手推车。

segments.text: Exercise can be a big help in avoiding ergonomic injuries.
segments.zh: 锻炼对避免人机工效伤害大有帮助。

segments.text: A regular exercise regimen will keep your body in good condition
segments.zh: 有规律的锻炼计划能让你的身体保持良好状态，

segments.text: and enable your muscles to do what you ask of them.
segments.zh: 使你的肌肉能够完成你要求它们做的事。

segments.text: It's also a good idea to start your day off with some warm-up stretches.
segments.zh: 每天开始时做一些热身伸展也是个好主意。

segments.text: And remember to do a few limbering exercises during your breaks.
segments.zh: 并且记得在休息时做几个舒展身体的练习。

segments.text: They should easily fit into your work schedule and help keep you comfortable
segments.zh: 它们很容易安排进你的工作日程，有助于让你

segments.text: throughout the day.
segments.zh: 一整天都感到舒适。

segments.text: You can help to eliminate ergonomic aches and pains by paying attention
segments.zh: 只要注意你的身体力学和工作环境，

segments.text: to your body mechanics and your work environment.
segments.zh: 你就能帮助消除人机工效方面的酸痛。

segments.text: Let's review.
segments.zh: 我们来回顾一下。

segments.text: Arrange your materials so that they're within easy reach.
segments.zh: 摆放好你的材料，让它们在伸手可及的范围内。

segments.text: Raise or lower work surfaces and position chairs and stools
segments.zh: 升高或降低工作台面，调整椅子和凳子的位置，

segments.text: so that you can use neutral positions.
segments.zh: 使你能够采用中立姿势。

segments.text: Avoid repetitive motions and take short breaks throughout the day.
segments.zh: 避免重复动作，并在一天中做短暂休息。

segments.text: Make sure that you have good lumbar support when you're sitting.
segments.zh: 坐着时确保有良好的腰部支撑。

segments.text: Practice good lifting habits.
segments.zh: 养成良好的搬举习惯，

segments.text: Lift with your legs, not with your back.
segments.zh: 用腿发力，而不是用背。

segments.text: And get plenty of exercise.
segments.zh: 并且多锻炼。

segments.text: It's easy to work ergonomically.
segments.zh: 符合人机工效地工作很容易，

segments.text: Just follow the rules and use common sense.
segments.zh: 只要遵守这些规则并运用常识，

segments.text: And you'll go home feeling great every day.
segments.zh: 你每天都会感觉很好地回家。
